=== 0e177c2655
Open every arriving file as a new project, except a drop on the canvas

Decided 2026-10-24 (agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md, "Opening and
importing files"). Before this, Home's Import button and a file opened
from Finder both added the file to whatever project was open behind
Home; a .3mf opened from Finder started a second JusPrin process; and a
.3mf dropped on a non-empty plate was silently cancelled, because the
file-load listener answers OrcaSlicer's "open as project or import
geometry?" dialog with Cancel.

What each way in does now:
- Opened from the OS (Finder/Explorer, "Open with", a second launch, the
  command line, a download handed to the app): a model file opens in a
  new project named after it and the app goes to Prepare; a .3mf opens
  as a project and asks "Previously opened file" when it was opened
  before.
- Home's Open… (was Import): the OS file dialog, then the same. Cancel
  leaves Home. Home's "+ New" is gone (File > New Project remains); the
  empty gallery says "Drop a model or project here, or Open…".
- Dropped on Home: the page sends each file's name and bytes (the web
  view takes the drop; by the wxWidgets source a native drop target on
  it would not see it on macOS, not tried with a real drag). The host
  writes them under <temp>/JusPrin-dropped/<MD5>/<name> and opens them
  as above, so a .3mf dropped twice is recognized the second time.
- Dropped on the Prepare canvas: a model file is added to the open
  project; a .3mf opens as a project with no project-or-geometry
  question.
- Add model… at the top of the Plates tab calls OrcaSlicer's add_model
  (File > Import). An empty Prepare canvas says "Drop a model here or
  add one".
- JusPrin runs as a single instance.

How: ShellController installs a handler on a new Plater seam and takes
the files OrcaSlicer's load_files(wxArrayString) is given. It leaves a
.3mf to OrcaSlicer (open_3mf_file -> load_project -> the existing
"Previously opened file" handler) and opens anything else in a new
project: OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::release_project (now public, the same
step the agent's project_open uses), then OrcaSlicer's own load. A
canvas drop must add, so the shell replaces OrcaSlicer's PlaterDropTarget
with its own; OrcaSlicer reinstalls its target after every slice, and
the shell puts its own back on the next idle. A lone zip keeps adding,
since File > Import > Import Zip Archive arrives the same way; Home opens
zips as new projects. The agent's tools load through overloads the seam
does not see, and the handler stands aside during a tool load.
attach_shell sets single_instance=true and project_load_behaviour=
load_all next to sync_system_preset; JusPrin's Preferences window does
not expose either.

Home protocol: import_project and new_project are replaced by open_file
and open_dropped_files. The version stays 1 (page and host ship
together). base64_decode moves from AgentHost.cpp into Support/Base64.hpp
so Home can decode dropped files.

Upstream-owned files: src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.hpp and Plater.cpp, 10 added
lines, none changed or deleted. A setter and member,
set_external_file_open_handler, mirroring set_external_project_open_handler,
and one call at the top of Plater::load_files(const wxArrayString&), after
the path filtering and the G-code checks and before the LoadFilesType
switch. Rebase note: keep the call before anything in that function that
adds to the model. The fork owns a neutral seam; the policy is in
ShellController. OrcaSlicer's PlaterDropTarget is not edited; the fork
installs its own target over it at runtime.
Rebase simulation: git merge-tree --merge-base=3ffb9585d2 upstream/main
(373ffaa13f) against this tree and against the parent 48c402949b. The
same files conflict in both. Plater.cpp has the same eight conflicts and
the new call merges cleanly. In Plater.hpp the setter lands inside the
existing conflict over the grouped JusPrin fork additions, whose natural
resolution (keep the fork's block) keeps it; the member merges cleanly.

Tests: jusprin_tests [home] (open_file routing, dropped files decoded and
undecodable ones left out), HomeUI Vitest (Open… sends open_file, no New,
a page drop sends name and bytes), and shell harness --file-arrival:
OS open on a project with an object -> new project, one object, Prepare;
canvas drop -> same project, +1 object, also after a slice; Home Open…
cancel stays on Home, a chosen file opens a new project; Home drop opens
a new project; a .3mf on a full plate asks the reopen question (the old
silent cancel) and opens the existing project; a .3mf canvas drop opens
as a project; the same .3mf dropped on Home twice asks the second time;
Add model… drawn above the plates. Removing the handler and load_all
makes the behavior checks fail; removing only the idle re-install makes
the after-slice canvas drop fail. --external-project-history (all
external_3mf_* and the agent project_open reopen checks) and
--reopen-prompt pass unchanged.

Live, in a re-signed copy with its own --datadir: two STLs opened with
`open -a` each landed in a new project in the running app; a .3mf did
too, in the same process, with no project-or-geometry question; opening
it again showed "Previously opened file". An instrumented Home page
showed Open… and no New, and its open_dropped_files opened a new
project while the resumed one kept its single object. A real drag onto
the canvas or Home, and Open…'s macOS dialog, were not driven live.


=== c7ea1d4a63
Fix the macOS build of ProjectStateDocument::calibration

48c402949b returns m_doc["calibration"] as std::optional<json>. Apple
clang (Xcode, macOS SDK 26.5) rejects the conversion as ambiguous: both
optional's converting constructor and json's templated conversion
operator to optional<json> match. Constructing the optional in place
names the one meant. No behavior change.
